action: Resolve application component ownership through a typed workspace_application_runtime record instead of the legacy WorkspaceRuntime candidate shape
necessity: A running application component deployment reported ownership=unregistered even though its workspace_application_runtime creation record was durably succeeded. WorkspaceRuntimeIdentityCandidates only accepts legacy workspace_runtime / workspace_launch_stage / ensure_runtime records and every consumer decodes those as a WorkspaceRuntime, so an application runtime - a different resource kind with a different record shape - was never matched. Ownership observation therefore could not prove which recorded operation created a running application workload. The fix adds a separate typed store query (WorkspaceApplicationRuntimeOwnerCandidates) and verifies the physical workload against the record that created it: account, workspace, runtime id, operation id, the request hash computed from the retained input, and the revision-declared component identity. Missing records stay unregistered; a corrupted record, a non-succeeded claim or an undeclared component fail closed as conflict; several components of one revision verify individually. Legacy runtime candidate semantics and consumers are untouched, so no existing ownership reader changes behavior, and the platform never guesses an owner for a workload it did not record.

checks: TestOverlayApplicationRuntimeDurableOwnerMiss reproduces the original miss and now resolves ownership=verified with an unchanged journal and zero provider mutation
Foreign identity, corrupted record and undeclared component each fail closed as conflict
An unowned workload and an unrecorded workload stay distinct
Every declared component of one revision verifies on its own identity, never as an owner conflict
The typed owner candidates round-trip through the memory store
The whole services/fabric/internal/fabric package passes database-free

remainingBoundary: Source-only verification with provider stubs and the in-memory store. The PostgreSQL restart proof for the new query (TestPostgresWorkspaceApplicationRuntimeOwnerCandidatesRestart) is included but needs a real database and runs in the full lane; no live cluster, provider procurement, production access, publication or deployment was performed.
